name: Abū ʿAmr Zabbān ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-Māzinī
summary: One of the seven readers of the Qurʾān and the great Basran authority on the speech and poetry of the Arabs, teacher of al-Khalīl, Yūnus and al-Aṣmaʿī.
bio: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ was a Basran of Māzin of Tamīm, one of the seven canonical readers of the Qurʾān, whose reading, through his student al-Yazīdī, is still recited in parts of Africa. He gathered the language and poetry of the Bedouin Arabs, and the sources say he burnt the notebooks he had filled when he turned to devotion. Al-Zubaydī counts him in the fourth generation of the Basran grammarians and again among the first lexicographers of Basra.

He was cautious with analogy and trusted what he had heard from the Arabs; the tradition contrasts him with Ibn Abī Isḥāq, who stretched analogy further, and tells that Ibn Abī Isḥāq once got the better of him on the hamza. His students al-Khalīl, Yūnus ibn Ḥabīb, al-Aṣmaʿī and Abū ʿUbayda carried the Basran learning of the next generation. He died in 154/771, on the way to Syria by some reports, near Kufa by others.
uncertain: His own name is given as Zabbān and in other forms; his year of death as 154/771 and also 157 or 159.
